name: Party Crasher
why: Bends the one rule everyone fears (a taken space) once; timing it is the decision and the victim saw it coming.

name: Alchemists
why: Quiet payment helper worth 3 for 5; nobody at the table notices it fire.

name: Extra Hand
why: Plain +1 minion once, at 9 cost it rarely beats a 9-follower buy.

name: Line Cutters
why: Worth 3 for 2 and overrides fewest-followers-first, so the leader keeps first pick: must-buy and anti-catch-up.

name: Old Maid
why: A poison card meant to be passed by swaps and gifts, but nobody recruits it, so it mostly rots in the shop.

name: Dabblers
why: Wild double member is a neat connector for color counts, but 'wild' needs a ruling on what it counts for.

name: Anarchist
why: Swap any two members anywhere each round: real table-wide aim, though rivals lose cards to it repeatedly.

name: Spoilsport
why: Cancel a contest you can't win: a clear block on the runaway leader with an obvious round-end moment.

name: Con Men
why: Big one-shot steal of 5; simple and felt, but it's just a bigger Accomplice with no color tie.

name: Sore Loser
why: Comeback steal from the top contest winner if you win nothing; pays the trailing seat.

name: Build Up
why: Plain green fuel anchor; nobody reacts, which is its job.

name: Echo
why: One sentence that reads the board and grows with whatever the last player took; blocking matters around it.

name: Reprise
why: Copy your own space: clean double-dip, but it only looks at your own minions.

name: Sample
why: Borrows a rival's best On Recruit; strong cross-color reach, needs a look at rival cards.

name: Cover
why: Copy an unclaimed space lets you take the blocked-for-later space early; real timing choice.

name: Greatest Hits
why: Round III payoff for a cult of On Recruit members; a visible engine finish.

name: Busker
why: Steady +2 green income; fine but invisible to the table.

name: Impersonator
why: Borrowing a rival's ability is fun, but which one it holds must be marked and remembered.

name: Impressionist
why: +1 resource when anyone copies: a small trigger nobody feels.

name: Wallflower
why: Doubling copied gains builds a real copy engine, but only for the rich and at 10 cost.

name: Fan Club
why: Copies the leader's space on arrival, a built-in catch-up aimed at the front-runner.

name: Roadie
why: Scales with green members, pure self-engine, nobody else notices.

name: Stunt Double
why: Copy the action you just took: simple double-dip that makes the space choice matter more.

name: Tribute Band
why: Doing a rival's whole round is a huge moment, but at 14 cost it's slow and can't be swapped back.

name: Doppelganger
why: Becomes a copy of your best member; solid but private, nobody at the table reacts.

name: Agents
why: A clean block against copiers, cheap; a counter card more than an engine.

name: Chronicler
why: Generic +1 per own-color member at game end, the same card several colors print.

name: Allowance
why: Same shape as Gather and Stash; adds nothing white-specific.

name: Splurge
why: Rewards pricey recruits; the 2-then-1 rate needs a moment's math.

name: Exchange
why: Straight resource-to-follower conversion; works, but nobody else cares.

name: Farewell
why: Cash a member out for its cost: clear, punchy, and combos with Martyrs and the pile cards.

name: Estate Sale
why: Farewell's twin paying white instead; repeats a sibling for less.

name: Cash In
why: Big round III conversion; solitaire, and rich-get-richer for whoever hoarded white.

name: Recluse
why: Pays the small cult at game end; a clean counter to wide play.

name: Landlord
why: Plain +2 white income, forgettable at the table.

name: Heiresses
why: 9 cost for a single small white burst; rarely worth it.

name: Brokers
why: Cheap 3-body that adds to White's own follower actions; nice engine piece, quiet.

name: Misers
why: Holding white for points; mild tension with spending it.

name: Raiders
why: Follower theft reads as Magenta's job pasted into White.

name: Cashier
why: Repeats Cash In on a member; no new angle.

name: Money Changers
why: Taxes everyone's follower buys a little; a quiet link to the core buy.

name: Martyrs
why: Makes stealing or swapping it backfire; links Red, Magenta and White's Farewell in one line.

name: Old Money
why: Generic per-own-color scorer, a sibling of Chronicler, Snobs and Timekeeper.

name: Hoarder
why: Turns a mixed pile into white once, setting up Cash In; a real timing call.

name: Help Yourself
why: The clean core steal; aim and split are real choices and the victims shrug.

name: Stash
why: Same shape as Gather and Allowance; no theft angle at all.

name: Lie Low
why: Small steal plus a round of safety: a visible block the table plays around.

name: Heist
why: Steal 3 followers: punchy and aimable at the leader.

name: Shake Down
why: The victim chooses their own punishment and loses either way; feels bad and reads awkwardly.

name: Poach
why: Take any rival's member in round III: a big clear finisher.

name: Cutpurse
why: Auto-aims at the richest rival so there's no decision, but it does check hoards.

name: Accomplice
why: Cheap 3-steal on arrival; simple and felt.

name: Grifter
why: Steal scales with cult size; rewards the wide leader.

name: Second-Story Man
why: Steal right before contests swings who wins a rim; the table watches for it.

name: Desperado
why: Bigger steals while trailing; real catch-up, but 'fewest followers' shifts turn to turn.

name: Extortionist
why: A pricier Cutpurse; repeats a sibling with no decision.

name: Bodyguards
why: Total steal immunity: a block that matters, but it's a wall, not an engine.

name: Double Agent
why: Swap itself for a rival's better member; a sting, though the rival gets a body back.

name: Kidnapper
why: Takes a rival's member every round from round I; the victim is robbed repeatedly with no choice.

name: Shoplifter
why: Steal on every recruit stacks with Red-style multi-recruits; a small but steady link.

name: Fence
why: Punishes stealers with magenta; a counter card, quiet unless a thief is at the table.

name: Savings
why: Blue income with an optional shop cycle; the bury-then-refill-then-recruit order takes a read.

name: Out of Style
why: Wipe a color from the shop: denies a rival's plan and pays you per card.

name: Peek
why: Ordering the pile is a real plan, but the outcome is hidden until you look.

name: Recruit Twice
why: Two buys in one turn: clear and strong at round II.

name: Bury
why: Deny one shop card for half its cost in blue; a clean hate-draft.

name: Spree
why: Three buys in round III, a big finisher.

name: Hawker
why: Rivals choose to overpay you or let you take it free: both sides weigh, but the text is long.

name: Patroness
why: Followers whenever shop cards are buried links Blue's spaces; unclear whether the round reset counts.

name: Snobs
why: Generic per-own-color scorer, a sibling of Chronicler and Timekeeper.

name: Window Shopper
why: Cycles the shop and pays colors; fine shop control.

name: Shopaholics
why: Two buys every turn is huge for whoever's already rich.

name: Window Dressers
why: A cheap 3-body with a small shop shuffle; repeats Window Shopper.

name: Doormen
why: Swap a rival's member for a shop card each round; the cost rule is wordy and hard to read cold.

name: Regular
why: +1 blue when you buy followers; nobody notices.

name: Trendsetters
why: Each recruit also buries a shop card, a quiet denial engine.

name: Critic
why: +1 follower when a rival recruits blue; a small trigger nobody feels.

name: Scavenger
why: Grab what a rival buries before it sinks; turns Blue's own bury spaces into a contest.

name: Harvest
why: Plain fuel in your colors; the yellow anchor.

name: Leaders' Tax
why: Pays for reading where rivals crowd; counting minions per color takes a beat.

name: New Blood
why: Rewards buying a new color; a plain choice of what to recruit.

name: Big New Blood
why: New Blood again, bigger; a sibling repeat.

name: Melting Pot
why: Scales with your color spread; a self-engine nobody else notices.

name: Makeover
why: Rearranging your pile in round III sets up contests and full sets in one move.

name: Gardeners
why: Fills your missing colors toward sets each round; cheap and catch-up shaped.

name: Customs Officer
why: +1 yellow when rivals steal or change your stuff; small and reactive.

name: Tourist
why: Followers per color held every round: visible, scaling, rewards going broad.

name: Harmonist
why: Game-end full-set scorer; ties to the contest but quiet.

name: Dyer
why: Tourist's shape paying yellow; repeats a sibling for less.

name: Meddler
why: Swapping each rival's resources hits contests table-wide, but 'one for one' into what color needs asking.

name: Drifters
why: Counts as any color: a flexible connector for color contests and New Blood.

name: Big Tent
why: Rewards one of each color; a real shape choice for your cult.

name: Caravan
why: Third member on the per-color-held shape; pricey and repetitive.

name: Tastemaker
why: Only Meddler changes rivals' resources, so it rarely fires.

name: Toast
why: Big silver with a small gift; clear, and the gift feeds rivals' silver contest.

name: Polish
why: Plain conversion; useful, unfelt.

name: Party Gifts
why: Gift silver for followers: everyone gains, and you choose whose contest you feed.

name: Potluck
why: Rivals pay a resource and get silver back; a mild, fair trade.

name: Sweet Talk
why: Silver plus free conversion; a fuel space with a twist nobody sees.

name: Largesse
why: Big round III gift-for-followers; aiming the gift at a contest is the play.

name: Godparent
why: Give a member away for its cost in followers; combos with Old Maid and Martyrs.

name: Hostesses
why: Small steady gifts for followers; fits but modest.

name: Caterer
why: +1 silver per gift; a small trigger.

name: Toastmaster
why: +1 follower on your own Silver spaces; dull.

name: Debutantes
why: Double your silver once, rivals get some: a strong contest swing with a timing call.

name: Smooth Talkers
why: Silver as any color is elegant, but at 11 cost it's untouchable and private.

name: Philanthropist
why: A small Largesse on a member; repeats the space.

name: Polisher
why: A once-per-game Polish; repeats a sibling.

name: Creditor
why: Buy 2 followers from a chosen rival for 3 silver each round; fair-ish and aimed.

name: Debt Collectors
why: Takes silver from everyone in a color about giving; off-theme.

name: High Society
why: Followers when rivals take Silver spaces: you profit from the color's own gifts.

name: Envy
hardFail: Relies on a rival having more resources than you
why: Pays only when a rival out-holds you in silver; also auto-math with no choice.

name: Sleep In
why: Big purple for going last; the Goes Last token rules take a read.

name: Hold Up
why: Skip the next turn, even your own: a clear sting with a real timing puzzle.

name: Right Away
why: Go again now; a simple tempo tool.

name: Last Call
why: Pays per minion left and pushes the rest last; strong but takes rereading.

name: Crunch Time
why: Three turns in a row lets you grab a cluster of spaces; clear power.

name: Overtime
why: +1 minion in round III; plain but useful.

name: Courier
why: Pays on double turns, combos with Right Away and snake ends; quiet.

name: Night Watch
why: Pays when rivals take Goes Last; needs the token rules to follow.

name: Night Owls
why: +1 minion each round from II; 'right away' after your last is a tricky timing read.

name: Early Birds
why: Cheap immunity to skips; a clean counter card.

name: Bouncers
why: Skip the next two rivals on arrival: a felt sting at a fair price.

name: Gossip
why: Follower per skip links Hold Up and Bouncers into an engine.

name: Timekeeper
why: Generic per-own-color scorer, a sibling of Chronicler and Snobs.

name: Closer
why: +4 purple for the last minion also helps win Went Last; doubles a reward for the same seat.

name: Hot Streak
why: Pays for a run of turns, but the table must count turns already gone.

name: Shift Crew
why: Vanilla 4 for 4 with no ability; nothing purple about it.

name: Night Shift
hardFail: Needs tracking a table can't do (which minions were placed before a skip)
why: A tangle of conditions nobody can read cold or remember at the table.

name: Tryout
why: Use a shop card's arrival effect without buying it; clever and reads the shop.

name: Gather
why: The Gather/Stash/Allowance shape; a recruit nudge.

name: Walk-In
why: Blind recruit from the pile with a gift to rivals; the allowed gamble.

name: Promote
why: Trade up with a rival or the shop; the victim gets a body back.

name: Demote
why: Trade down to get a cheap card plus red; useful twin.

name: Initiation
why: Free member up to 8 in round III; a clean finisher.

name: Body Snatchers
why: Equal-cost swap every round: aimed and fair-ish.

name: Volunteer
why: Vanilla 1-cost body; swap fodder only.

name: Mentor & Protégés
why: Recruit a second card free on arrival; a strong red engine piece.

name: Proselytizers
why: +1 follower per recruit; steady and private, rewards the wide leader.

name: Mob
why: Big round-end payout for red width; 12 cost and win-more.

name: Recruiter
why: Proselytizers paying red; a sibling repeat.

name: Patriarch
why: Generic members-count scorer; rewards the wide leader.

name: Greeters
why: A small bonus on On Recruits that needs a reread to place.

name: Deprogrammers
why: A follower sting on every swap or steal; cheap for worth 4.

name: Panel
why: A built-in Promote or Demote on arrival; on theme and aimable.

name: Loyalists
why: Swap immunity for your cult; a counter card the table must route around.

name: Clerk
why: +1 red each round; forgettable.
